title: Lemon
summary: A Rust project that connects Telegram commands to Solana transactions. It explores async request handling, transaction signing, and RPC interaction.
detail: Uses Tokio to process bot updates and sign Solana transactions through a chat interface.
overview: Most Telegram wallet bots feel clunky or hide how transactions are built. I wrote Lemon in Rust to explore how a chat interface can act as a wallet adapter, similar in spirit to Phantom or Backpack. It receives Telegram updates, constructs Solana instructions, simulates transactions against an RPC node, and signs them.

decisions.title: Async update handling with Tokio
decisions.body: Telegram bot updates arrive concurrently. Using Tokio tasks keeps slow RPC network calls from blocking new messages from other users.

decisions.title: Transaction simulation before signing
decisions.body: Before submitting a transfer or program call, the bot runs a pre-flight RPC simulation so failed instructions are caught and reported clearly in chat.

decisions.title: Separated command parser and signer
decisions.body: Keeping chat command parsing separate from Ed25519 signing logic makes it easier to test Solana transaction builders without running a live Telegram webhook.

title: Solana On-Chain Programs
summary: A set of Rust programs on Solana covering a tokenized vault (ERC-4626 style), a two-party token escrow, and delegated spending allowances.
detail: Built with Rust and Anchor using Program Derived Addresses (PDAs) and SPL Token CPIs.
overview: To understand how Solana handles state and account permissions on-chain, I implemented several core financial primitives in Rust. The repository includes a vault program modeled after Ethereum's ERC-4626 standard, an escrow program for atomic token swaps, and an allowance program for delegated token transfers.

decisions.title: PDA vault custody
decisions.body: Each vault and escrow state account uses deterministic Program Derived Addresses (PDAs) as token authority, so only the program itself can sign outgoing SPL token transfers.

decisions.title: Checked integer math for vault shares
decisions.body: Calculating deposit shares and withdrawal amounts uses checked arithmetic in Rust to prevent integer overflow or rounding bugs.

decisions.title: Explicit account constraints
decisions.body: Every instruction verifies token mint ownership, signer privileges, and account relationships before modifying balances.

title: Wiki Backend
summary: A community platform backend for tracking shared tasks and learning progress, using PostgreSQL, SQLx, and WebSockets for live updates.
detail: Combines REST endpoints for persistence with WebSocket rooms for real-time task state.
overview: Wiki was built for a 'learning in public' community where members share tasks and progress updates. Instead of polling the server for changes, the backend pairs PostgreSQL storage with WebSocket rooms so task updates appear immediately for everyone connected.

decisions.title: Compile-time checked SQL with SQLx
decisions.body: Using SQLx allows queries to be checked against the PostgreSQL schema at compile time, catching column or type mismatches before deployment.

decisions.title: Room-based WebSocket broadcasts
decisions.body: When a user updates a task over HTTP or WebSocket, the server commits the change to Postgres and broadcasts the event to active connections in that room.

decisions.title: Simple connection pooling
decisions.body: Shared database connection pools keep request latency steady when multiple clients load feeds and update tasks at the same time.

title: Solana Token Launchpad
summary: A web tool for creating SPL tokens on Solana, setting token metadata, and configuring mint authorities in a single wallet transaction.
detail: Assembles mint account creation and initialization instructions on the client with web3.js.
overview: Creating a new SPL token on Solana involves several separate instructions: allocating the mint account, initializing decimals and authorities, creating an associated token account, and minting initial supply. This web app bundles those steps into one transaction signed through a browser wallet.

decisions.title: Single-transaction batching
decisions.body: Combining account creation and mint initialization into one atomic transaction prevents partial state if a user rejects or drops a second prompt.

decisions.title: Client-side wallet adapter integration
decisions.body: Uses the Solana Wallet Adapter so users sign directly with their own wallet without exposing keys to a backend server.

title: Endroite
summary: A Telegram bot built with TypeScript and Node.js that automates adding custom audio tracks and visual effects to uploaded images and videos.
detail: Processes media streams asynchronously and cleans up temporary buffers after delivery.
overview: Endroite is a utility bot for Telegram that takes user-uploaded photos or video clips, applies preset visual filters and background audio tracks, and replies with the finished video file. It was an exercise in handling media streams and child processes cleanly in Node.js.

decisions.title: Queued media jobs
decisions.body: Video encoding uses significant CPU and memory, so incoming requests are queued rather than spawned all at once.

decisions.title: Automatic temp file cleanup
decisions.body: Each job writes to an isolated temporary path and removes intermediate files whether encoding succeeds or fails.
